    Icons are Material Symbols. The default class is material-symbols; it uses the outlined family. Ligature names come from the Material Symbols catalog.

    The framework does not ship the font files. Outlined, rounded, and sharp are three separate variable fonts — bundling them would dwarf the rest of the CSS. Load the families you actually use, with the axis ranges so fill / weight / grade / optical size work. Outlined alone is enough for the default.

    Icons inherit the current text color, so token utilities such as primary-text work. For icons inside buttons, see Buttons.

    {% endcall %} {% call section("style", "Style") %}

    Outlined, rounded, and sharp are font families, not variation axes. Set the icon-style attribute — the same idea as theme — or set --md-icon-font directly. Either one inherits, so a subtree can use a different style.

    {% endcall %} {% call section("axes", "Axes", heading="Fill, weight, grade, optical size") %}

    These four are variable-font axes. They inherit, so set them on :root or on a wrapper. A missing range in the Google Fonts URL (a link without opsz,wght,FILL,GRAD@…) serves a static instance and the axes will not move.

    Token Default Range
    --md-icon-fill 0 0 or 1
    --md-icon-weight 400 100–700
    --md-icon-grade 0 −50–200
    --md-icon-optical-size 24 20–48 (unitless)
    {% call code() %} :root { --md-icon-fill: 0; --md-icon-weight: 400; --md-icon-grade: 0; --md-icon-optical-size: 24; } favorite {% endcall %}

    icon-filled is a shortcut for --md-icon-fill: 1.
